stem: Dev has saved \$46 and earns \$12 per hour at a part-time job. What is the least number of whole hours he must work so that his total savings are at least \$315?
solution: Let \(h\) be the number of hours: \(46 + 12h \ge 315\).
22 hours is not quite enough (\(46 + 264 = 310\)), so he needs 23 whole hours.

explanation.A: Incorrect. This rounds \(22.41...\) down; after 22 hours Dev has only \(46 + 12(22) = 310\) dollars, less than \$315.
explanation.B: Correct. \(46 + 12h \ge 315\) gives \(h \ge 22.41...\), so 23 is the least whole number of hours.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This ignores the \$46 already saved: \(12h \ge 315\) gives \(h \ge 26.25\), so 27.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This adds the \$46 to the goal instead of subtracting it: \(12h \ge 361\) gives 31.

verify:
h = symbols('h')
s = solve_univariate_inequality(46 + 12*h >= 315, h, relational=False)
assert s == Interval(Rational(269, 12), oo)
least = ceiling(Rational(269, 12))
assert least == 23 and value(choices[answer]) == least
assert all(value(choices[k]) != least for k in choices if k != answer)
